title: Cross-stitch single daisy
subtitle: A fresh white daisy with a golden centre on 14-count green Aida
excerpt: A single oxeye daisy stitched in white, cream and yellow on 14-count sage green Aida. The design is approximately 55 by 55 stitches and finishes at about 10 by 10 cm. The coloured background removes the need for any background stitching and gives the finished piece a botanical illustration quality.
sourceNotes: Original design. The oxeye daisy (Leucanthemum vulgare) is native to Britain and northern Europe. Stitching on coloured Aida is a standard design approach in UK cross-stitch publishing.

glossaryTerms.definition: The number of stitching squares or thread intersections per inch on the fabric. 14-count Aida has 14 stitching squares per inch; 18-count Aida has 18. A higher count produces finer, smaller stitches.

content.text: Sage green Aida works as the stem and background simultaneously. The petals are stitched without any background fill needed, keeping the stitch count low and the result clean. A 14-
fabric gives a finished size that fits in a 12 cm hoop for display.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 3865 (white), ECRU, 745 (very light pale yellow), 744 (medium pale yellow), 972 (deep canary), 310 (black), 3011 (dark khaki green), 3012 (medium khaki green)

content.text: Stitch the petals from the outside in.
Each petal uses 3865 for the outer two-thirds and ECRU for the inner third closest to the centre. Stitch all petals before filling the centre.
The centre disc uses 972 as the main fill with 744 and 745 as graduated inner zones. The centre disc is roughly circular, approximately eight stitches in diameter.
The stem uses 3011 in a single vertical line of back-stitch. The leaves use 3012 for the main fill and 3011 for the mid-rib line.
Add French knot texture to the flower centre.
Work a ring of French knots in 310 around the outer edge of the centre disc to create the shadow zone typical of an oxeye daisy centre.
Leave in the 12 cm hoop and wrap the excess Aida neatly behind. The sage green Aida framed in a natural wood hoop makes a clean display piece.
